paper.abstract:
Abstract. String graphs are intersection graphs of continuous curves in the plane.
In 2010, Fox and Pach proved that string graphs with m m edges admit balanced vertex separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m 3 / 4 ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m}) and conjectured that this bound can be improved to 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) , which would be optimal.
After partial progress, Lee claimed in 2017 to prove this conjecture, and more generally to prove analogous separator theorems for region intersection graphs over minor-closed graph families.
A key intermediate step in Lee’s approach was a padded decomposition scheme for region intersection graphs.
In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Lee’s approach to the broader setting of graph classes excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor.
These results have since found applications in a wide range of works. Later in 2024, a flaw was discovered in the construction of Lee’s padded decomposition scheme, invalidating Lee’s as well as Korhonen and Lokshtanov’s separator results, and many works relying on them. In this work, we prove that string graphs with m m edges admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) , and more generally obtain analogous 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) bounds for region intersection graphs over fixed minor-closed graph families and for graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor, thereby repairing the vast majority of the affected works.
Furthermore, our balanced separators can be found in polynomial time. Our proof uses a different approach from Lee’s and does not rely on padded decompositions.
Since padded decompositions have also found applications independent of the separator theorems, particularly for string graphs, we also prove a padded decomposition result for region intersection graphs that is optimal for string graphs. We have formalized both the balanced separator and the padded decomposition results in Lean 4 with mathlib.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.text: In 1979, Lipton and Tarjan [ 35 ] showed that every n n -vertex planar graph admits a balanced separator – a set whose removal breaks the graph into small pieces – of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( n ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}) . This bound is optimal (up to constant factors) since the n × n \sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n} grid is planar and does not admit a balanced separator of size o ⁡ ( n ) o(\sqrt{n}) . Since the seminal work of Lipton and Tarjan, balanced separators have been a central object of study in graph theory and theoretical computer science, with applications in many different areas, most notably algorithm design [ 36 , 4 , 43 , 16 , 17 , 26 ] . In particular, sublinear balanced separators have been shown to exist for various graph classes. For example, graphs of genus g g admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( g ​ n ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{gn}) [ 22 ] and graphs that exclude K h K_{h} as a minor admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( min ⁡ { h ⋅ n + f ⁡ ( h ) , h ​ log ⁡ h ⋅ n } ) \mathcal{O}\bigl(\min\bigl\{h\cdot\sqrt{n}+f(h),\>h\sqrt{\log h}\cdot\sqrt{n}\bigr\}\bigr) , for a fast-growing function f f [ 3 , 23 , 32 ] . Note that the latter result also applies to all classes excluding an h h -vertex graph as a minor. Another way of generalizing the separator result is to look at classes of graphs defined by intersecting geometric objects. For a family 𝒮 \mathcal{S} of objects, typically compact and connected subsets of ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} , their intersection graph has a vertex for every object in 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , and an edge exists if and only if the corresponding objects intersect. For example, Miller, Teng, Thurston, and Vavasis [ 39 ] showed that disk graphs (i.e., intersection graphs of disks in the plane) admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( ω ​ n ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\omega n}) , where ω \omega is the maximum size of a clique in the graph. We remark that the dependence on ω \omega cannot be dropped, since the complete graph K n K_{n} is a unit disk graph, and does not admit a balanced separator of size o ⁡ ( n ) o(n) . The above result of Miller et al. was later extended to more general intersection graphs of fat, similarly-sized objects [ 44 ] , and to sparse intersection graphs of related objects [ 20 ] . What about intersection graphs of arbitrary connected subsets of the plane, also known as string graphs ? Here we cannot hope for a balanced separator of size o ⁡ ( n ) ⋅ f ⁡ ( ω ) o(n)\cdot f(\omega) , for any function f f , since the complete bipartite graph K n , n K_{n,n} is a string graph and has no sublinear separators. However, in 2010, Fox and Pach [ 19 ] proved that string graphs with m m edges admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m 3 / 4 ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m}) . They also conjectured that this bound can be improved to 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) . Conjecture 1.1 (Fox and Pach [ 19 ] ) . Every m m -edge string graph admits a balanced separator of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) . Note that this would be optimal since every planar graph is a string graph and its number of edges is linear in the number of vertices. In 2013, Matoušek [ 38 ] improved the separator size to 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}\log m) , almost closing the gap, and in 2017, Lee [ 33 ] claimed to finally prove Conjecture 1.1 . Actually, Lee did not work with string graphs, but with more general region intersection graphs . We say that a graph G G is a region intersection graph over a graph H H if vertices of G G can be mapped to connected subsets of H H so that G G is the intersection graph of these subsets. Lee claimed the following result. Theorem 1.2 . For every h ⩾ 1 h\geqslant 1 there exists a constant c h c_{h} with the following property. Every m m -edge region intersection graph over a K h K_{h} -minor-free graph admits a balanced separator of size at most c h ⋅ m c_{h}\cdot\sqrt{m} . Lee’s argument yields c h = 𝒪 ⁡ ( h 3 ​ log ⁡ h ) c_{h}=\mathcal{O}(h^{3}\sqrt{\log h}) . As string graphs are exactly region intersection graphs over planar graphs [ 28 ] , which are K 5 K_{5} -minor-free, Theorem 1.2 immediately implies Conjecture 1.1 . In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Theorem 1.2 to the even broader setting of induced-minor-free graph classes [ 27 ] . We say that a graph H H is an induced minor of a graph G G if H H can be obtained from G G by a sequence of vertex deletions and edge contractions. A graph is H H -induced-minor-free if it does not contain H H as an induced minor. Let K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} denote the 1 1 -subdivision of K h K_{h} , bisecting every edge exactly once. By directly using some intermediate results of Lee as a black box, Korhonen and Lokshtanov claimed a form of the following result. Theorem 1.3 . Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be an m m -edge graph excluding K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} as an induced minor. Then G G admits a balanced separator of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( min ⁡ ( log ⁡ m , h 2 ) ⋅ h ⋅ m ) . \mathcal{O}\left(\min\bigl(\log m,h^{2}\bigr)\cdot h\cdot\sqrt{m}\right){.} Furthermore, there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph G G , either obtains such a balanced separator or concludes that G G contains K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} as an induced minor. In the latter case, there is a second Las Vegas randomized polynomial-time algorithm that produces an induced minor model of K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} in G G . We note that if G G is a region intersection graph over a K h K_{h} -minor-free graph, then G G is K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} -induced-minor-free. On the other hand, for every h h , there is a K 6 ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{6}^{(1)}} -induced-minor-free graph that is not a region intersection graph over any K h K_{h} -minor-free graph [ 9 ] . Thus, Theorem 1.3 is a strict generalization of Theorem 1.2 . Over the years, many different papers have built on these results, as well as the different intermediate results [ 8 , 41 , 40 , 31 , 30 , 37 , 7 , 5 , 45 ] . Unfortunately, in 2024, a significant error was discovered in a core component of Lee’s original proof of Theorem 1.2 [ 9 ] , invalidating or weakening key results in the follow-up work. (Following [ 9 ] , the inequality at the sixth line of the proof of Lemma 4.14 of the full version of Lee’s paper [ 33 ] need not hold.) In this paper, we present a new proof of Theorem 1.3 that does not rely on the flawed component of Lee’s proof. As previously noted, our result implies Theorem 1.2 and thus proves Conjecture 1.1 . As a consequence, we also fix the majority of papers that were broken by the invalidation of Lee’s result. Our proof uses two standard ideas via a multicommodity flow framework shared by much of the previous work [ 38 , 33 , 27 ] . First, we apply a multicommodity flow bound proven by Korhonen and Lokshtanov [ 27 ] to show that the graph admits a multicommodity flow of value Ω ⁡ ( m ) \Omega(\sqrt{m}) , whose dual form gives us a vertex-weighted metric over the graph. Second, we construct a metric embedding into the line. It is in the details of this second idea that our techniques diverge somewhat from Lee’s methods, so the intermediate results we obtain are not all identical. In Section 8 we list results relying on the work of Lee and discuss whether and how they are fixed by our results.

( ⋆ \star ) If G G is a region intersection graph over a graph G 0 G_{0} that excludes K h K_{h} as a minor, then for every assignment of vertex weights w : V → ℝ ⩾ 0 w\colon V\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0} , the endpoint-light vertex-weighted shortest-path metric d w G d_{w}^{G} admits an ( 𝒪 ⁡ ( h 2 ) , Ω ⁡ ( 1 ) ) \bigl(\mathcal{O}(h^{2}),\Omega(1)\bigr) -padded decomposition scheme. An embedding f : X → ℝ f\colon X\to\mathbb{R} of ( X , d ) (X,d) into the line is said to be non-expansive if | f ⁡ ( x ) − f ⁡ ( y ) | ⩽ d ⁡ ( x , y ) |f(x)-f(y)|\leqslant d(x,y) for all x , y ∈ X x,y\in X . It should be noted that every finite metric space with n n points admits a Rabinovich embedding with (average) distortion 𝒪 ⁡ ( log ⁡ n ) \mathcal{O}(\log n) [ 18 , Theorem 3.1] . As a corollary of ( ⋆ \star ), Lee (implicitly) claimed the following result on Rabinovich embeddings. Theorem 1.5 . Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be a region intersection graph over a K h K_{h} -minor-free graph G 0 G_{0} , and let w : V → ℝ ⩾ 0 w\colon V\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0} be an assignment of vertex weights. Then the endpoint-light vertex-weighted shortest-path metric d w G d_{w}^{G} admits a non-expansive embedding into the line with average distortion at most 𝒪 ⁡ ( h 2 ) \mathcal{O}(h^{2}) . We will prove the following result, that in particular implies Theorem 1.5 as a special case. Theorem 1.6 . Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be a graph excluding K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} as an induced minor, and let w : V → ℝ ⩾ 0 w\colon V\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0} be an assignment of vertex weights. Then the metrics d w G d_{w}^{G} and d ¯ w G \smash[t]{\overline{d}}_{w}^{G} admit non-expansive embeddings into the line with average distortion min ⁡ { 𝒪 ⁡ ( log ⁡ | V | ) , 625 ​ h 2 } . \min\left\{\mathcal{O}(\log{|V|}),\>625h^{2}\right\}{.} Furthermore, there is a polynomial-time in | V | |V| algorithm that, given a graph G G and an assignment of vertex weights w : V → ℝ ⩾ 0 w\colon V\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0} , obtains either an induced minor model of K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} in G G , or such a non-expansive embedding into the line. This will be enough to prove Theorem 1.3 and, consequently, Theorem 1.2 , as well as fix a number of prior works building on Lee’s. However, we believe that ( ⋆ \star ) should hold as well, even in the more general setting of forbidden induced minors, and even for a stronger parameter dependence generalizing an analogous result for K h K_{h} -minor-free graphs [ 12 ] . To this end, we pose the following conjecture. Conjecture 1.7 . Let G G be a K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} -induced-minor-free graph, and let w : V → ℝ ⩾ 0 w\colon V\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0} be an assignment of vertex weights. Then the endpoint-light vertex-weighted shortest-path metric d w G d_{w}^{G} admits an ( 𝒪 ⁡ ( log ⁡ h ) , Ω ⁡ ( 1 ) ) \bigl(\mathcal{O}(\log h),\Omega(1)\bigr) -padded decomposition scheme.

sections.heading: Other Related Works
sections.text: In late 2025, Davies [ 14 ] and, independently, Chang, Conroy, Tan, and Zheng [ 10 ] proved that every unweighted string graph admits an embedding into an edge-weighted planar graph that preserves all pairwise shortest-path distances up to a universal constant factor. We emphasize that these results do not resolve Conjecture 1.1 : they apply to unweighted shortest-path metrics, whereas Lee’s approach requires padded decompositions for vertex-weighted shortest-path metrics. In fact, vertex-weighted string graphs do not admit embeddings into planar graphs with universally bounded distortion, as we show in Appendix A .

sections.heading: Formalization
sections.text: To avoid further errors, we have formalized the existential statements in Theorem 1.3 , Theorem 1.4 , and Theorem 1.8 in Lean 4 with mathlib. Our formalization of these first two results was almost entirely constructed using the proprietary LLM-based tool Aristotle [ 2 ] (with some small manual edits, and other small edits using a coding agent), although we have carefully separated the definitions and main theorem statements from the proofs, and carefully hand-verified them so that we can be confident in the result. The improved bound was formalized using GPT 5.6 Sol. We note that the formalization differs very slightly in some of its proof details compared to what we present in this paper, and also in its constants. However, all asymptotic dependencies on n n , m m , and h h are the same. Our formalization is publicly available. 4 4 4 https://github.com/jacketsj/formalized-induced-minor-free-separators

sections.heading: 8. Conclusion: Impact on Previous Works
sections.text: As the main results of this paper, we proved Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 that were previously stated, respectively, by [ 33 ] and by Korhonen and Lokshtanov [ 27 ] . We also proved Theorem 1.4 that fixes the result ( ⋆ \star ) claimed by Lee [ 33 ] , but with weaker parameters. In this section, we go over papers building on Theorem 1.2 , Theorem 1.3 , and the result ( ⋆ \star ) or their respective proofs, and we discuss whether or not (and how) they have been fixed as a result of our work.

sections.heading: Results Directly Using Separator Theorems
sections.text: A number of papers [ 8 , 41 , 40 , 5 ] used the separator theorems of Lee [ 33 ] as black boxes, usually to design divide-and-conquer algorithms. We remark that in typical cases, exchanging the separator of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) to one of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}\log m) , given by Matoušek [ 38 ] makes the running time only slightly worse. Nevertheless, with Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 reproven, the results claimed in these papers are now fully fixed. Similarly, de Berg, Jansen, and Lamme [ 15 ] did not use the results of Lee since they were already aware of the mistake, and thus they used the weaker 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}\log m) separator. With Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 reproven, the results claimed in this paper can now be slightly improved.

sections.heading: Results Directly Using Padded Decompositions
sections.text: The main result of the paper A Constant Factor Approximation for Navigating Through Connected Obstacles in the Plane by Kumar, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, and Suri [ 31 ] directly relied on ( ⋆ \star ), but was needed only for string graphs. Thus, the result is now fixed by Theorem 1.4 . Similarly, in the paper Point Separation and Obstacle Removal by Finding and Hitting Odd Cycles by Kumar, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, Suri, and Xue [ 30 ] , one of the main results for the “obstacle removal” problem directly relied on ( ⋆ \star ) for string graphs and is wholly fixed by Theorem 1.4 . Now let us go back to the paper that started it all, i.e., Separators in Region Intersection Graphs by Lee [ 33 ] . As an application of the padding decomposition scheme, Lee showed a result concerning eigenvalue bounds for region intersection graphs. For a graph G G with degree-vector d → \vec{d} and adjacency matrix A A , its Laplacian matrix is L := diag ⁡ ( d → ) − A L:=\operatorname{diag}(\vec{d})-A , and the eigenvalues of L L are denoted λ 1 ​ ( G ) ⩽ λ 2 ​ ( G ) ⩽ ⋯ ⩽ λ n ​ ( G ) \lambda_{1}(G)\leqslant\lambda_{2}(G)\leqslant\cdots\leqslant\lambda_{n}(G) . Lee [ 33 , Theorem 1.11] claimed that for any graph G G with maximum degree Δ \Delta that is a region intersection graph over another graph G 0 G_{0} , where G 0 G_{0} is K h K_{h} -minor-free, λ k ​ ( G ) = 𝒪 ⁡ ( Δ 2 ​ h 6 ​ log ⁡ h ) ​ k | V G | \lambda_{k}(G)=\mathcal{O}(\Delta^{2}h^{6}\log h)\frac{k}{|V_{G}|} . The proof applied ( ⋆ \star ) in full generality, and so we recover a weaker bound via Theorem 1.4 . The resulting bound is the same up to factors depending on h h . In particular, if h h is a constant, then the bound is λ k ​ ( G ) = 𝒪 ⁡ ( Δ 2 ) ​ k | V G | \lambda_{k}(G)=\mathcal{O}(\Delta^{2})\frac{k}{|V_{G}|} . Lee applied the methods of Kelner, Lee, Price, and Teng [ 24 ] for this proof, and it seems quite likely that these results could be derived using only the weaker notion of Rabinovich embeddings, but we leave this to future work.

sections.heading: Results Using Klein-Plotkin-Rao Decomposition
sections.text: Finally, let us discuss the so-called Klein-Plotkin-Rao (KPR) decomposition [ 25 ] (sometimes called a low-diameter decomposition). Originally shown for K h K_{h} -minor-free graphs, this result says that we can remove a small fraction of vertices so that any two vertices in the same component of the resulting graph are close to each other in the original graph. Lee [ 33 ] claimed that an analogous result holds for string graphs, and, more generally, graphs excluding a fixed induced minor. The KPR decomposition for string graphs and induced-minor-free graphs was later used in the paper A 1.9999 1.9999 -Approximation Algorithm for Vertex Cover on String Graphs by Lokshtanov, Panolan, Saurabh, Xue, Zehavi [ 37 ] , as well as the (first version of) the preprint Treewidth is Polynomial in Maximum Degree on Graphs Excluding a Planar Induced Minor by Bonnet, Hodor, Korhonen, and Masařík [ 7 ] . For the string graph results in the first paper, the required theorems [ 37 , Theorems 5 and 9] follow from applying our Theorem 1.4 with unweighted shortest-path metrics using essentially-unchanged proofs. Note that the string representation is not required since we may use an approximation algorithm of Krauthgamer and Roughgarden [ 29 ] . Their results also extend to region intersection graphs over K h K_{h} -minor-free graphs in this manner, but extending them to induced-minor-free graphs via an analogous low-diameter decomposition result remains an open problem.

String graphs are intersection graphs of continuous curves in the plane. In 2010, Fox and Pach proved that string graphs with m m edges admit balanced vertex separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m 3 / 4 ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m}) and conjectured that this bound can be improved to 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) , which would be optimal. After partial progress, Lee claimed in 2017 to prove this conjecture, and more generally to prove analogous separator theorems for region intersection graphs over minor-closed graph families. A key intermediate step in Lee’s approach was a padded decomposition scheme for region intersection graphs. In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Lee’s approach to the broader setting of graph classes excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor. These results have since found applications in a wide range of works. Later in 2024, a flaw was discovered in the construction of Lee’s padded decomposition scheme, invalidating Lee’s as well as Korhonen and Lokshtanov’s separator results, and many works relying on them. In this work, we prove that string graphs with m m edges admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) , and more generally obtain analogous 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) bounds for region intersection graphs over fixed minor-closed graph families and for graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor, thereby repairing the vast majority of the affected works. Furthermore, our balanced separators can be found in polynomial time. Our proof uses a different approach from Lee’s and does not rely on padded decompositions. Since padded decompositions have also found applications independent of the separator theorems, particularly for string graphs, we also prove a padded decomposition result for region intersection graphs that is optimal for string graphs. We have formalized both the balanced separator and the padded decomposition results in Lean 4 with mathlib. 1. Introduction In 1979, Lipton and Tarjan [ 35 ] showed that every n n -vertex planar graph admits a balanced separator – a set whose removal breaks the graph into small pieces – of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( n ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}) . This bound is optimal (up to constant factors) since the n × n \sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n} grid is planar and does not admit a balanced separator of size o ⁡ ( n ) o(\sqrt{n}) . Since the seminal work of Lipton and Tarjan, balanced separators have been a central object of study in graph theory and theoretical computer science, with applications in many different areas, most notably algorithm design [ 36 , 4 , 43 , 16 , 17 , 26 ] . In particular, sublinear balanced separators have been shown to exist for various graph classes. For example, graphs of genus g g admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( g ​ n ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{gn}) [ 22 ] and graphs that exclude K h K_{h} as a minor admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( min ⁡ { h ⋅ n + f ⁡ ( h ) , h ​ log ⁡ h ⋅ n } ) \mathcal{O}\bigl(\min\bigl\{h\cdot\sqrt{n}+f(h),\>h\sqrt{\log h}\cdot\sqrt{n}\bigr\}\bigr) , for a fast-growing function f f [ 3 , 23 , 32 ] . Note that the latter result also applies to all classes excluding an h h -vertex graph as a minor. Another way of generalizing the separator result is to look at classes of graphs defined by intersecting geometric objects. For a family 𝒮 \mathcal{S} of objects, typically compact and connected subsets of ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} , their intersection graph has a vertex for every object in 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , and an edge exists if and only if the corresponding objects intersect. For example, Miller, Teng, Thurston, and Vavasis [ 39 ] showed that disk graphs (i.e., intersection graphs of disks in the plane) admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( ω ​ n ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\omega n}) , where ω \omega is the maximum size of a clique in the graph. We remark that the dependence on ω \omega cannot be dropped, since the complete graph K n K_{n} is a unit disk graph, and does not admit a balanced separator of size o ⁡ ( n ) o(n) . The above result of Miller et al. was later extended to more general intersection graphs of fat, similarly-sized objects [ 44 ] , and to sparse intersection graphs of related objects [ 20 ] . What about intersection graphs of arbitrary connected subsets of the plane, also known as string graphs ? Here we cannot hope for a balanced separator of size o ⁡ ( n ) ⋅ f ⁡ ( ω ) o(n)\cdot f(\omega) , for any function f f , since the complete bipartite graph K n , n K_{n,n} is a string graph and has no sublinear separators. However, in 2010, Fox and Pach [ 19 ] proved that string graphs with m m edges admit balanced separators of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m 3 / 4 ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m}) . They also conjectured that this bound can be improved to 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) . Conjecture 1.1 (Fox and Pach [ 19 ] ) . Every m m -edge string graph admits a balanced separator of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}) . Note that this would be optimal since every planar graph is a string graph and its number of edges is linear in the number of vertices. In 2013, Matoušek [ 38 ] improved the separator size to 𝒪 ⁡ ( m ​ log ⁡ m ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m}\log m) , almost closing the gap, and in 2017, Lee [ 33 ] claimed to finally prove Conjecture 1.1 . Actually, Lee did not work with string graphs, but with more general region intersection graphs . We say that a graph G G is a region intersection graph over a graph H H if vertices of G G can be mapped to connected subsets of H H so that G G is the intersection graph of these subsets. Lee claimed the following result. Theorem 1.2 . For every h ⩾ 1 h\geqslant 1 there exists a constant c h c_{h} with the following property. Every m m -edge region intersection graph over a K h K_{h} -minor-free graph admits a balanced separator of size at most c h ⋅ m c_{h}\cdot\sqrt{m} . Lee’s argument yields c h = 𝒪 ⁡ ( h 3 ​ log ⁡ h ) c_{h}=\mathcal{O}(h^{3}\sqrt{\log h}) . As string graphs are exactly region intersection graphs over planar graphs [ 28 ] , which are K 5 K_{5} -minor-free, Theorem 1.2 immediately implies Conjecture 1.1 . In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Theorem 1.2 to the even broader setting of induced-minor-free graph classes [ 27 ] . We say that a graph H H is an induced minor of a graph G G if H H can be obtained from G G by a sequence of vertex deletions and edge contractions. A graph is H H -induced-minor-free if it does not contain H H as an induced minor. Let K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} denote the 1 1 -subdivision of K h K_{h} , bisecting every edge exactly once. By directly using some intermediate results of Lee as a black box, Korhonen and Lokshtanov claimed a form of the following result. Theorem 1.3 . Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be an m m -edge graph excluding K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} as an induced minor. Then G G admits a balanced separator of size 𝒪 ⁡ ( min ⁡ ( log ⁡ m , h 2 ) ⋅ h ⋅ m ) . \mathcal{O}\left(\min\bigl(\log m,h^{2}\bigr)\cdot h\cdot\sqrt{m}\right){.} Furthermore, there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph G G , either obtains such a balanced separator or concludes that G G contains K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} as an induced minor. In the latter case, there is a second Las Vegas randomized polynomial-time algorithm that produces an induced minor model of K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} in G G . We note that if G G is a region intersection graph over a K h K_{h} -minor-free graph, then G G is K h ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{h}^{(1)}} -induced-minor-free. On the other hand, for every h h , there is a K 6 ( 1 ) \smash[t]{K_{6}^{(1)}} -induced-minor-free graph that is not a region intersection graph over any K h K_{h} -minor-free graph [ 9 ] . Thus, Theorem 1.3 is a strict generalization of Theorem 1.2 . Over the years, many different papers have built on these results, as well as the different intermediate results [ 8 , 41 , 40 , 31 , 30 , 37 , 7 , 5 , 45 ] . Unfortunately, in 2024, a significant error was discovered in a core component of Lee’s original proof of Theorem 1.2 [ 9 ] , invalidating or weakening key results in the follow-up work. (Following [ 9 ] , the inequality at the sixth line of the proof of Lemma 4.14 of the full version of Lee’s paper [ 33 ] need not hold.) In this paper, we present a new proof of Theorem 1.3 that does not rely on the flawed component of Lee’s proof. As previously noted, our result implies Theorem 1.2 and thus proves Conjecture 1.1 . As a consequence, we also fix the majority of papers that were broken by the invalidation of Lee’s result. Our proof uses two standard ideas via a multicommodity flow framework shared by much of the previous work [ 38 , 33 , 27 ] . First, we apply a multicommodity flow bound proven by Korhonen and Lokshtanov [ 27 ] to show that the graph admits a multicommodity flow of value Ω ⁡ ( m ) \Omega(\sqrt{m}) , whose dual form gives us a vertex-weighted metric over the graph. Second, we construct a metric embedding into the line. It is in the details of this second idea that our techniques diverge somewhat from Lee’s methods, so the intermediate results we obtain are not all identical. In Section 8 we list results relying on the work of Lee and discuss whether and how they are fixed by our results. Padded Decompositions and Metric Embeddings As mentioned, a key step in the original claimed proofs of both Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 is to use a lemma of Lee’s that gives a certain kind of metric embedding into the line. To this aim, Lee made use of so-called padded decompositions for vertex-weighted shortest-path metrics. Padded decompositions have seen a number of (effectively equivalent) definitions. We use the one by Conroy and Filtser [ 12 ] . Other Related Works In late 2025, Davies [ 14 ] and, independently, Chang, Conroy, Tan, and Zheng [ 10 ] proved that every unweighted string graph admits an embedding into an edge-weighted planar graph that preserves all pairwise shortest-path distances up to a universal constant factor. We emphasize that these results do not resolve Conjecture 1.1 : they apply to unweighted shortest-path metrics, whereas Lee’s approach requires padded decompositions for vertex-weighted shortest-path metrics. In fact, vertex-weighted string graphs do not admit embeddings into planar graphs with universally bounded distortion, as we show in Appendix A .
